source.title: AI Ethics Principles
source.publisher: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
source.reference_note: Printed page numbers and Annexure C checklist IDs refer to the official PDF. Checklist IDs below were verified against Annexure C; they are references, not app control IDs or an official scoring rubric.

principles.name: Fairness
principles.rationale: The use-case context, data considerations, fairness assessment, validation plan, and monitoring plan provide places to document potential differential impacts and planned responses.
principles.coverage: FAI-01 records affected groups, fairness risks, evaluation approach and limitations, observations, mitigations, owner, reviewer, and assessment status. An optional nested evaluation record can document selected groups, dataset context, metric definitions, proposed thresholds and rationale, subgroup results, test outcome, evidence references, limitations, and review roles. MAP-01 and intake add purpose and affected-people context; MON-01 includes planned disparity monitoring.
principles.gaps: The optional FAI-01 evaluation record is user-entered documentation, not an independently verified statistical assessment. It does not establish metric suitability, dataset representativeness, threshold appropriateness, subgroup result validity, or operational monitoring outcomes. No official SDAIA score or pass threshold is implemented.
principles.limitations: A completed or Reviewed form does not establish that a fairness evaluation was performed or that outcomes are fair.

principles.name: Privacy & Security
principles.rationale: Use-case and data context, privacy/data governance documentation, and security assessment prompts support a documentary view of privacy and security considerations.
principles.coverage: DAT-01 records data categories, purpose and necessity, minimisation, sensitive-data use, access, retention/deletion, risks, mitigations, owner, and reviewer. SEC-01 documents security scope, risks, access controls, data protection, third parties, planned monitoring, and escalation.
principles.gaps: There is no structured evidence of data classification or provenance, de-identification, consent or rights handling, completed security testing, or operational privacy/security monitoring.
principles.limitations: These records are not a privacy impact assessment, legal review, proof of controls operating, or evidence that security testing occurred.

principles.name: Humanity
principles.rationale: Intake and related assessments capture purpose, affected people, decision role, human oversight, validation planning, and incident correction considerations relevant to human-centered use.
principles.coverage: Intake records affected people, potential impact, AI role, and oversight. TRN-01 and VAL-01 describe oversight, while INC-01 includes human review and correction of affected decisions.
principles.gaps: There is no dedicated assessment of fundamental rights, KSA cultural values, freedom of choice, or documented impact and remedy analysis.
principles.limitations: Human-oversight descriptions are proposed governance documentation; they do not demonstrate effective human intervention in an operating system.

principles.name: Social & Environmental Benefits
principles.rationale: Purpose, affected people, fairness considerations, and planned monitoring can help frame social impacts, but the existing control set does not provide a dedicated social/environmental assessment.
principles.coverage: Use-case intake captures intended purpose, affected people, and potential impact; FAI-01 and MON-01 provide limited places to describe impacts on affected groups.
principles.gaps: No explicit social or environmental benefit/harm assessment, sustainability indicators, resource or energy measures, or rationale for non-applicability is collected.
principles.limitations: The mapping does not assert that the example use case produces social benefits or has been assessed for environmental impact.

principles.name: Reliability & Safety
principles.rationale: Security assessment, validation planning, monitoring plans, and incident-response planning provide documentation points for reliability, safety, escalation, and recovery considerations.
principles.coverage: VAL-01 captures validation scope, criteria, approach, test-set considerations, findings/evidence, oversight, and limitations. MON-01 records planned metrics, thresholds, frequency, ownership, and escalation; INC-01 describes triage, containment, correction, and recovery.
principles.gaps: No structured evidence specifically records unexpected/extreme-scenario testing, fallback tests, system-failure test results, or completed stakeholder sign-off.
principles.limitations: Plans and fields do not prove technical robustness, safe operation, completed tests, or production performance.

principles.name: Transparency & Explainability
principles.rationale: Use-case context, transparency documentation, and planned monitoring and incident records provide limited documentation of system purpose, limitations, communication, feedback, and issue handling.
principles.coverage: TRN-01 records purpose, AI decision role, users and stakeholders, limitations, oversight, information to communicate, disclosure approach, and outstanding actions. MON-01 includes complaint indicators; INC-01 includes incident documentation.
principles.gaps: No evidence establishes delivered disclosures, decision-level explanations or traceability, explanation testing, accessibility, or a user-feedback process and its outcomes.
principles.limitations: Recording an intended communication approach is not evidence that affected people were informed or can understand or challenge an outcome.

principles.name: Accountability & Responsibility
principles.rationale: The inventory/use-case ownership and RACI baseline, together with named assessment owners/reviewers and lifecycle plans, offer traceability points for responsibility and governance roles.
principles.coverage: GOV-01 draws on inventory and RACI baselines; intake records a business owner; structured evidence records responsible owners and reviewers. RACI identifies roles for use-case approval, risk, privacy, security, monitoring, incidents, and independent assurance.
principles.gaps: The RACI editor is not persisted. The app does not establish appointed entity-level SDAIA roles, completed independent audits, third-party contractual due diligence, training, or implemented redress mechanisms.
principles.limitations: A role matrix and readiness result do not evidence approval, audit, legal accountability, effective redress, or conformity with SDAIA requirements.
